questions.stem: A robotics team applies PCA and then K-means to an unlabeled feature matrix. Which interpretation correctly qualifies the PCA entry in the slide’s Clustering box?

options.text: PCA supplies cluster membership, whereas the later clustering step merely changes the coordinate axes.
Both steps necessarily assign the same groups because neither requires ground-truth class labels.
PCA supplies a principal-component representation; the separate clustering step supplies group membership.
PCA requires class labels, whereas only the later clustering step can operate on unlabeled observations.

solution.justification: The source correctly introduces structure in unlabeled data and grouping by clustering, but places PCA inside its Clustering box. The official PCA documentation identifies centered-data linear dimensionality reduction. In the stipulated two-stage pipeline, PCA transforms the feature representation and clustering assigns groups. The slide placement is retained as a caveat rather than taught as an algorithm taxonomy.

optionExplanations.o1: PCA is a linear dimensionality-reduction method. Group assignment is the stated purpose of the separate clustering stage; membership in an unsupervised-learning category does not make the operations identical.
optionExplanations.o2: This exchanges the roles: a PCA projection is not itself a set of cluster labels.
optionExplanations.o3: PCA does not require ground-truth class labels for its standard unsupervised dimensionality-reduction role.
optionExplanations.o4: The lack of labels is shared context, not proof of identical outputs or grouping.

solution.simpleExplanation: A projection changes how observations are represented; clustering decides which observations belong together.
solution.memoryAid: Projection gives coordinates; clustering gives groups.
misconceptions: Unsupervised does not mean clustering, and a PCA projection does not automatically supply cluster labels.
examTraps: Unsupervised does not mean clustering, and a PCA projection does not automatically supply cluster labels.

conflictResolution.sourceClaim: PCA is visibly listed in the Clustering box.
conflictResolution.qualification: PCA is dimensionality reduction, not itself a clustering algorithm. Preserve its slide placement as a source caveat and test clustering labels versus projection.
conflictResolution.primaryEvidenceScope: Official current PCA class documentation was opened and read; it describes centered-data linear dimensionality reduction. No install or PCA execution was needed.
conflictResolution.method: Keep the source claim visible; assess only the explicitly qualified distinction. This draft is not an approval or a claim that the underlying source wording has changed.
